title: Sarah Martin as a sister; her sister in Baltimore; her teeth
summary: She calls Sarah Martin her sister, mentions a sister who is a doctor in Baltimore, and talks about her sore gums.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I see, okay. Would you tell me something about Sarah Martin (PHONETIC)?
I can tell you that she was my sister, she called me her sister, her baby sister. I got another girl my sister too, in Baltimore.

You know, since I had that tooth pulled, my gums are sore, you know, and I had to take me -- I did have them on when you come, before you come, but them things hurt me. I took them out. I tried to have them on when you come. I said, "Oh, these things hurt me." I took them out.
Do you put them in when you sing? Do you put your teeth in when you sing?
I had (unintelligible) but I just had my teeth pulled and -- Monday, when I (inaudible).
Well, yes. I always have them (unintelligible) and I just took my (inaudible).
